name: Sesame
one_liner: Cash-pay marketplace where you book a video visit with a therapist, psychiatric prescriber or doctor at a price shown upfront. No insurance billing.
best_for: People without insurance or with high-deductible plans who want an upfront price
People who need a quick psychiatric visit or non-controlled medication refills
People who want to pick a specific provider by price and availability
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who need stimulants, benzodiazepines or other controlled medications
People who want their insurance billed directly
short_description: Cash-pay telehealth marketplace. Each provider sets a visit price shown before booking; Mental Health Rx medication management is $79/month.
long_description: Sesame is a US marketplace for cash-pay health care. You browse independent providers, see each one's price upfront, and book a video (or some in-person) visit; it covers mental health along with urgent care, prescriptions, weight loss and other services. For mental health you can book therapy sessions or psychiatric visits with a psychiatrist or psychiatric nurse practitioner, or join Mental Health Rx, a $79/month subscription for ongoing medication management with refills and provider messaging. Sesame does not bill insurance, though you can submit receipts yourself for out-of-network reimbursement. Its providers do not prescribe controlled substances such as stimulants (Adderall, Vyvanse) or benzodiazepines, and it does not have psychiatrists in every state. Visits tend to be one-off bookings, so ongoing therapy with one clinician depends on that clinician's availability. Sesame also sells a medication membership, Everyday Rx (see the SesameRx record).
patient_summary: You pick a provider on Sesame, see their price before you book, and pay by card for a video visit; prices vary by provider and location. For ongoing psychiatric medication, Mental Health Rx costs $79/month. Sesame does not take insurance and its providers can't prescribe controlled substances like Adderall or Xanax.

pricing.starting_price: Price set by each provider, shown before booking; Mental Health Rx $79/month
pricing.notes: Pay per visit at the provider's listed price (varies by provider and location). Mental Health Rx: $79/month for ongoing medication management (refills, messaging, video visits). Optional Sesame Plus membership gives visit discounts (reported $10.99/month or $99/year by ChoosingTherapy; confirm on Sesame). Costco members get lower prices. No insurance billing; you can submit receipts for out-of-network reimbursement.

privacy.notes: Policy says Sesame may share personal information with third parties for their direct marketing (California residents can opt out) and share de-identified data with advertisers. Provider terms require health data to be kept under HIPAA. Deletion rights for all users not confirmed. No regulatory action found.

seo.meta_description: Sesame Care offers affordable cash-pay therapy ($75-130) and psychiatry ($100-175). No insurance accepted. Cannot prescribe controlled substances.

faqs.a: No. Sesame is cash-pay only. You pay upfront and can submit the receipt to your insurance for potential out-of-network reimbursement, but Sesame doesn't bill insurance directly. This keeps prices transparent but means no copay benefits.

faqs.q: How much does therapy cost on Sesame?
faqs.a: $75-130 per session, with most therapists charging around $104. Prices vary by provider and state. You see the exact price before booking. No hidden fees.

faqs.q: How much does psychiatry cost on Sesame?
faqs.a: $100-175 for follow-up visits, but initial psychiatric consultations can run $250-350 depending on location. The $79/month Mental Health Rx subscription is worth considering if you need ongoing medication management.

faqs.q: Can Sesame psychiatrists prescribe Adderall or Xanax?
faqs.a: No. Sesame providers cannot prescribe controlled substances including stimulants (Adderall, Vyvanse, Ritalin), benzodiazepines (Xanax, Klonopin, Ativan, Valium), or opioids. You'll need a different provider for these medications.

availability.note: US only. Psychiatrists are not available in every state; primary care providers may prescribe some mental health medications instead.
